edge_gate.summary: Without the gate the deterministic agent trades 188 times instead of 53; the extra trades lose to the close at the same rate per contract, so CLV $ falls from -19 [-36, -1] to -82 [-121, -48] (paired difference -63 [-104, -32]). With the sceptic, the reasoner agent goes from 2 to 3 trades: it proposes 110 orders at edge 0 and the sceptic vetoes 107 of them (69 of 70 low-edge ones), so it still holds the line without the gate.

adaptive_edge.verdict: Given an edge ladder, the agent learned to *raise* its threshold: from base 4¢ the gate accepted 10¢ on 26 Feb (held-out CLV $ −9.54 → −4.83 over 16 changed trades) and rejected a later move down to 3¢; the 10¢ rule expired after its 45 days on 12 Apr. That beats no learning by +$21 CLV [+4, +38] (p = 0.011), but it only edges the published split-gate learner, by +$3 [+0, +6], with P&L indistinguishable (−$6 [−199, +198]). It wins the same way the published learner does: by trading less (42 vs 53 vs 129 trades), not by finding better trades. CLV per contract stays negative (−0.45¢) and its CI still covers the other arms. Starting lower (1¢) lets the learner climb only to 5¢ and later drop back, ending at 80 trades and −$29, worse than the published learner. Conclusion: a learned threshold is a safe, slightly better replacement for the fixed 7¢ template, not a source of edge; consistent with `edge_gate.md`, the M4 gap does not predict CLV.

forecast_blend.intro: `agents/forecast_blend.py`: p(home) = sigmoid(Σ w_k · logit(signal_k)), w on the simplex, so a one-hot weight on *anchor + M4 shift* is the published agent. After each settled test day the learner refits w on settled games only (exponentiated gradient on log loss, L2 pull toward the current weights) and a split gate accepts the proposal only if **Brier (primary metric, fixed up front)** on held-out earlier days improves by ≥ 0.0005. Windows: gate days = the 7 market days before the last 7; fit = the other days of the last 42; the first review needs 21 settled days. Starting weights: one-hot on anchor + M4 shift.

forecast_blend.reading: the blend trades about as often as the agent but loses less CLV per contract; the CLV-dollar gain survives real quotes (an earlier run on approximate quotes, 1 h mid ± 1¢, gave +$19 [+2, +37]), while P&L is indistinguishable. Part of the gain can come from the 1 h mid input pulling the estimate toward the traded price (fewer, smaller disagreements with the market). The forecast gain is not significant: Brier −0.0010 vs the agent, and still behind anchor + MLP alone and the market at tip.
forecast_blend.final_weights: anchor 0.03, mid 0.13, anchor_m4 0.07, anchor_mlp 0.67, anchor_gru 0.05, m4 0.01, mlp 0.03, gru 0.01

improves: **Fewer trades, and that is most of the gain.** A makes 53 trades for CLV -18.7 $ (mean -0.42¢ per contract). The reasoner with the sceptic (D) makes 2 (+3.9 $). Its +22.7 $ over A splits into +17.7 $ from skipping 52 of A's trades, +5.0 $ from one added trade (a 14¢ longshot, 142 contracts) and +0.0 $ on the one trade both made. Any filter that keeps 2 of A's trades gets the skipping part: random 2 of 53 gives -0.7 $ [-3.7, +2.5].

**D's 2 trades beat 2 random trades from A, but on n = 2.** Mean CLV +1.00¢ vs random -0.42¢ (p = 0.16 that random is at least as good); CLV $ +3.9 vs random [-3.7, +2.5] (the $ is driven by the contract count of one cheap longshot).

**The sceptic's vetoes lean the right way, not significantly.** Of C's 42 reasoner trades, the 40 vetoed averaged -0.47¢ and the 2 kept +1.00¢: kept − vetoed +1.47¢ [-1.27¢, +4.25¢]; a random 2 of 42 does at least as well 12% of the time.

**Explainability and auditability.** Every LLM trade carries a rationale that cites tool outputs, the citations are machine-checked against those outputs, and the sceptic's reasons name a concrete concern (stale 24-hour anchor, price already moved, no news behind the edge) — A's brief only shows the numbers.
worse: **No better selection among A's trades.** The reasoner tool agent (C) keeps 20 of A's trades and drops 33: kept -0.45¢ vs dropped -0.41¢ (kept − dropped -0.04¢ [-1.05¢, +0.82¢]); a random keep of the same size is at least as good 54% of the time. The 22 trades it adds average -0.36¢, the same as A. On outcomes (noisy) the kept A trades won 20% vs 52% for the dropped ones. D's one kept A trade was -1.50¢.

**No better forecasts than the market.** The plain LLM's home-win probabilities beat A's Brier score (chat -0.0058 [-0.0129, +0.0000]) only because they copy the current mid (mean distance 0.13 points); vs the mid itself: -0.0007 [-0.0017, +0.0000]. "Moving toward the close" is just moving to the market, which already sits near the close: more conservative, not more informed.

**Tool-agent estimates are more overconfident than A's.** On its 51 buy proposals the reasoner's estimate sits +9.4¢ above the mid for the side it buys (A at the same points: +4.5¢); the closing price moved -0.0¢.

**Reliability, latency, cost.** 14% of reasoner tool-agent decisions were invalid (empty/malformed JSON, often after spending the reasoning budget; 9 buy proposals failed the citation check), all treated as passes. The reasoner tool agent needs 28 s of LLM time per decision and $1.05 per trade with the sceptic; A runs in milliseconds for free. The guardrails (checks and risk limits) never had to block either agent.

model_review.verdict: The model-review subloop proposed a different forecast six times (four logistic stacks, two M6), each the lowest-Brier blend on its 7 selection days, and the held-out CLV gate rejected all six. So the agent kept anchor + M4 shift all season, and in the full replay the arm is identical to the current agent: 53 trades, CLV $ −18 [−34, −2], P&L −96 [−437, +247]; paired difference +0 [+0, +0].

cards.name: M1a rolling average / M1b gradient boosting
cards.predicts: A player's points and minutes as quantiles (10/25/50/75/90%).
cards.inputs: M1a: the player's last 10 games. M1b: recent form plus teammates-out, rest and opponent features.
cards.architecture: M1a: rolling quantiles. M1b: gradient-boosted trees, one per quantile.
cards.training: Player games before 1 Feb 2026; held-out test from 1 Feb.
cards.trading: Baselines for M2; not used by the trader.

cards.name: M2 GRU (deep learning)
cards.predicts: A player's points and minutes as quantiles (10/25/50/75/90%).
cards.inputs: Last 20 games × 7 columns (min, pts, fga, fta, started, home, rest_days) plus a mask, and 17 static features (rest, teammates out, opponent pace, ...).
cards.architecture: GRU (64) over the sequence → concat static → MLP 64, ReLU, dropout 0.1 → 2 targets × 5 quantiles (monotone via softplus increments); pinball loss.
cards.metric: Points pinball 1.553 vs 1.590 (M1b) / 1.641 (M1a); coverage points 80.9%, minutes 80.0%.
cards.trading: Not in the trader: M4's missing-minutes/points inputs already carry absent players' usual output.

cards.name: M3 play model
cards.predicts: Probability a player plays in the next game.
cards.inputs: Availability features for every player on the team's recent roster, as of tip.

cards.name: M4 win model (logistic regression)
cards.predicts: P(home team wins) given who is out.
cards.inputs: rating_diff, margin10_diff, rest_diff, b2b_diff, missing_min_diff, missing_pts_diff. Rating: exponentially weighted margin (half-life 10 games, shrunk with 3 pseudo-games); absences counted for rotation players (≥ 15 min, played within 14 days).
cards.architecture: Logistic regression, C = 1. Coefficients: intercept +0.2342, rating +0.1309, margin10 -0.0148, rest -0.03648, b2b -0.2882, missing_min +0.006439, missing_pts -0.02248.
cards.metric: Brier 0.1827, accuracy 74.1%, AUC 0.801 on 501 test games (Kalshi at tip: 0.1633).
cards.trading: Its news shift (after news − before news) is added to the 24 h market anchor: the published agent's estimate. Known flaw: the shift's 'before' uses out=[], double-counting absences already known at anchor time.

cards.name: M4-NN MLP / GRU
cards.inputs: MLP: M4's six features. GRU: each team's last 10 games plus the six features.
cards.architecture: MLP 6 → 16 → 1; GRU hidden 8; chosen on 1 Dec – 31 Jan validation; 3-seed mean.
cards.training: Games before 1 Feb 2026 (early stopping on Dec–Jan, then refit).
cards.metric: Brier 0.1842 (MLP) / 0.1864 (GRU); anchor + MLP shift 0.1632, the best forecast we have.
cards.trading: A signal in the forecast blend and a candidate in model review; never adopted by the full agent.

cards.name: M6 ImpactNet
cards.predicts: How much the home price moves between now and tip.
cards.inputs: Recent price moves, spread, volume, anchor, move since anchor, hours to tip, news flags.
cards.architecture: Small neural net over the recent price sequence plus static features.
cards.metric: Null result: MAE 0.867¢ vs 0.833¢ for predicting no move (+0.033¢ [+0.021, +0.045]).
cards.trading: M6 agent placed 0 trades; both M6 proposals in model review were rejected.

cards.name: Forecast blend
cards.predicts: P(home wins) as a weighted log-odds average of 8 signals.
cards.inputs: anchor, mid, anchor_m4, anchor_mlp, anchor_gru, m4, mlp, gru.
cards.architecture: Simplex weights, refit daily on settled games (exponentiated gradient); a gate accepts a refit only if held-out Brier improves by ≥ 0.0005.
cards.training: Walk-forward over the test period, settled games only.
cards.metric: Brier 0.1654; 6 updates accepted. Final weights: anchor 0.03, mid 0.13, anchor_m4 0.07, anchor_mlp 0.67, anchor_gru 0.05, m4 0.01, mlp 0.03, gru 0.01.
cards.trading: Simplified offline trader only; not wired into the full agent.

cards.name: In-play model
cards.inputs: Pre-game probability, live score margin, time remaining, news margin.
cards.architecture: Brownian-motion (diffusion) model of the margin, σ = 14 points per game.
cards.training: σ fixed; pre-game prior from M4.
cards.trading: Not used in any published trading result.

cards.name: Plain LLM as a forecaster
cards.predicts: P(home wins) from one prompt with quotes, anchors, news and M4.
cards.inputs: The same as-of information block as the agent.
cards.architecture: DeepSeek chat / reasoner, one call, no tools.
cards.metric: Brier 0.1603 (chat) vs 0.1610 for the current mid; mean distance to the mid 0.0013: it essentially copies the market.
cards.trading: Arm B on the 40% subsample (3–5 trades).

takeaways: **No model beats the market at forecasting.** M4 alone scores Brier 0.1827; the best model-plus-market estimate (Anchor + MLP shift, 0.1632) only ties Kalshi at tip (0.1633).
**Anchoring on the market cuts the losses**: P&L after fees goes from −$2,087 (raw M4, no agent) to −$247 (anchor agent), full test period.

**Every safety or learning layer helps the same way: by trading less.** Split-gate learning, the learned edge threshold, the 4¢ edge gate and the LLM sceptic all improve CLV by cutting trades, not by picking better ones.

**Better Brier ≠ better trading.** The learned blend gains +$18 [+4, +33] CLV only on a simplified trader (P&L −$4 [-365, +378], no difference). Inside the full agent, model review proposed 6 lower-Brier forecasts and the CLV gate rejected 6: the agent kept anchor + M4 (53 trades, CLV $ -18 [-34, -2], same as the published agent).

**The best deep-learning results are the player models**: M2 GRU points pinball 1.553 vs 1.590 for the best M1 baseline; M3 Brier 0.1433 vs 0.1686. Next step: earlier information (official injury reports) rather than a better model.
